Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Emma McLeod and Kate Irwin walk in with their blades for New Zealand Women Under-19. Nthabiseng Nini has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the conditions at the venue appear to favor the bowlers, setting the stage for an intriguing chase. With the South African total providing a par total, the New Zealand batters will need to navigate the challenging conditions effectively. Which side will come out on top? We shall find out together. Chase coming up shortly...

Jemma Botha is in for a chat. She says that she just kept on going and the coach had told them that the start was important and they had a lot of training before this game. Ends by saying that they think they have a good total on the board.

Following Botha's dismissal, the South African batting lineup struggled to maintain a high run rate, ultimately posting a par total of 91 runs in the rain-curtailed 11-over-per-side contest. Karabo Meso played a good cameo towards the end. The New Zealand bowlers, particularly Ayaan Lambat, made a significant impact in the latter stages of the innings. Lambat's impressive spell yielded three crucial wickets, including the important scalp of Jemma Botha.

So South Africa Women Under-19 ended up with a par total of 91 on the board. They made a promising start to their innings, with both openers displaying solid form. However, Lourens' unlucky dismissal for 21 halted their momentum. Jemma Botha continued to play aggressively, but her departure in the 8th over for 32 runs marked a turning point in the innings.

OUT! TAKEN! Slower one, on off, Diara Ramlakan moves forward to loft it but the ball hits the upper part of her bat. It carries towards mid off. Anika Todd moves forward and takes a comfortable catch. South Africa Women Under-19 end their innings at 91/7!

New Zealand Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Emma McLeod, Kate Irwin, Eve Wolland, Anika Todd, Tash Wakelin (C), Kate Chandler, Darcy Prasad (WK), Ayaan Lambat, Louisa Kotkamp, Rishika Jaswal, Sophie Court.

South Africa Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Simone Lourens, Jemma Botha, Diara Ramlakan, Kayla Reyneke (C), Karabo Meso (WK), Fay Cowling, Mieke van Voorst, Luyanda Nzuza, Ashleigh van Wyk, Monalisa Legodi, Nthabiseng Nini

Kayla Reyneke, the skipper of South Africa Women Under-19, says that they also would have bowled first but they are ready for the challenge. Adds that they are not used to the conditions but they are excited for the game.
Tash Wakelin, the skipper of New Zealand Women Under-19, says that they will bowl first and just can't wait to get out and play some cricket.
TOSS - New Zealand Women Under-19 have won the toss and will BOWL first.
Good news! The game is set and it will be an 11-over per side game.

Meanwhile, Chelsea and Manchester City trail behind, while Forest and in-form Newcastle remain in contention, with Forest just two points behind Arsenal.

You guys can also switch tabs and enjoy the coverage between Pakistan and West Indies Test match live from the Multan Cricket Stadium. After a rocky start, Saud Shakeel and Mohammad Rizwan provided stability, although both batters narrowly missed out on centuries. Following their departures, the Pakistani innings succumbed rapidly.

After posting a competitive total of 144 runs, England's hopes of securing a victory were dashed when rain intervened. Ireland had begun their chase, but their progress was halted inside just four overs, with the loss of two wickets. This will undoubtedly be a disappointment for England, as they were looking for a strong start to their campaign, but unfortunately, the points were shared.
Still waiting for an official update from the Borneo Cricket Ground. Fingers crossed for some good news! We'll share it with you as soon as we get it. Stay tuned!

As we wait for the toss to happen, here's what happened in the first game of the ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2025 between Australia Women Under-19 and Scotland Women Under-19. The Aussies made a strong statement, dominating Scotland in all aspects. Scotland struggled to make an impact with the bat and were bundled out for a mere 48 runs, with the Australian bowlers, Eleanor Larosa and Caoimhe Bray taking three wickets each! In reply, Australia's Kate Pelle lit up the proceedings with an explosive first over, smashing three sixes, and alongside Ines McKeon, as they quickly chased down the modest Scottish total. They chased down the total inside 7 overs with 9 wickets in their kitty.

Karabo Meso is in for a chat now. She says that she was ready for the game but unfortunately, it is raining. Adds that they had a good start in the warm up game against India and they are excited for this game.

Emma McLeod is in for a quick chat. She says that it has been a long morning and hopefully they will get a game. Adds that they trust their side and she is excited about the game and says that hopefully, it happens.

Welcome to the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup, where the excitement is building as New Zealand Women Under-19 take on South Africa Women Under-19 in their opening match!
... MATCH DAY ...

The ICC U-19 Women’s T20 World Cup kicks off in Malaysia, with New Zealand Women Under-19 opening their campaign against South Africa Women Under-19. Both teams are eager to set the tone for their tournament, making this a contest to watch. New Zealand, semi-finalists in the previous edition, are bolstered by the return of key players Tash Wakelin, Kate Chandler, Louisa Kotkamp, Emma McLeod, and Kate Irwin. Wakelin, an off-spinning all-rounder and the leading wicket-taker in last year’s National U-19 tournament, will captain the side. Adding firepower, seven players from Auckland Cricket’s National U-19 tournament-winning team are in the mix, including leg-spinner Rishika Jaswal, the 2024 Girls First XI Cup MVP, who shared this honor with McLeod in 2023. The Kiwis had a mixed warm-up campaign, winning one game and losing another. While their top order, led by McLeod and Irwin, remains their backbone, the middle-order trio of Eve Wolland, Anika Todd, and Darcy Prasad could be pivotal. On the bowling front, they boast a well-rounded attack with a blend of pace and spin, which shone in the practice games. South Africa Women Under-19, led by Western Province all-rounder Kayla Reyneke, arrive with confidence after a strong warm-up victory over India U-19 Women via the DLS method. Their squad blends experience and young talent, with seven players returning from the inaugural tournament. Standouts include leg-spinner Seshnie Naidu and wicketkeeper Karabo Meso, both of whom have senior international experience. Diara Ramlakan, previously a reserve, has earned her place in the main squad this time. South Africa’s batting looks solid with Simone Lourens and Deidre van Rensburg being crucial at the top, while their bowling unit led by the pacy Monalisa Legodi, features both variety and depth, is ready to challenge the Kiwis. Their spirited showing in warm-ups will give them the belief to shine on the big stage. With both sides packed with potential match-winners, this promises to be an electrifying encounter. Can the Kiwis maintain their momentum from the last edition, or will South Africa’s all-round strength give them the edge? Let’s find out!
